engines_compared: Mem0, Nemori, LightMem, Memori, Hindsight, Honcho

areas.title: 1. Turn rewriting and decontextualisation at ingest
areas.question: Does the engine rewrite turns into standalone facts, and from what unit (turn, window, episode)?
areas.memspine_has: Window facts (`write.window_extract=facts`), envelope with one repair, grounding check, temporal anchoring stage W2-14, coverage re-extract W2-15, episode section (window mode `all`). Read-time `[= date]` annotation. Lift derived hits to source turns (`read.lift_before_rerank`, S15). Screens S03/S04/S43-S45/S62.
areas.gap: MemSpine writes facts straight from raw turns and retrieves them as competing records; the two best vendor LoCoMo systems (EverOS 93.5, Mem0 platform 92.5) retrieve a larger unit (episode, or memory plus source chunk) and use facts as keys. The window-facts arms regress on their own, so the open question is the unit that is returned, not the quality of the fact text. The replay-date defect (Mem0 OSS, Memori, Nemori facts) is a known trap that MemSpine must keep tested.

engine_table.approach: ADD-only 15-80-word self-contained facts from both speakers; sees top-10 existing memories; relative dates resolved against an Observation Date, but OSS refuses a caller timestamp so replayed history is dated with the run date
Batch LLM segmenter, then per-group third-person episode narrative with absolute dates in parentheses; then predict-calibrate extracts only the facts the prediction missed

Two stages: episode text per MemCell first (dual date 'last Friday (2023-05-12)'), atomic facts then extracted from the episode, stored with parent_id; the episode is the retrieved unit, facts ride along
Session chunked into semantic blocks; atomic memories resolve ambiguous references per chunk; the original chunk stays attached and is injected on a hit
'Lossless restatement' per entry: third person, no pronouns, relative to ISO absolute; speaker labels discarded by the builder
Narrative facts with what/when/where/who/why in one text; event date in the prompt, occurred_start/end returned; entities and causal links from the same call
Explicit atomic 'conclusions', pronouns resolved, peer id as subject, absolute dates from message time
Standalone facts with source_id per topic segment; LoCoMo prompt separates mention time from event time; entry_type tag is lost on insert (defect)
Long self-contained third-person statements (key/value/tags); window summary copied into a 'background' field of each fact
Observer turns raw messages into dated, prioritised observations that REPLACE the messages; 3-6x compression
Per-batch episodic event with LLM occurred_at; harness prepends date-resolution instructions
window_extract: atomic dated facts quoting a verbatim span, rejected if uncited; window facts alone lost on LoCoMo (S03 -4, S04 -6); S62 bundle queued

areas.title: 2. Entity, alias and coreference linking
areas.question: How are mentions linked to one identity, and where does coreference get resolved?
areas.memspine_has: Full ladder, rules/llm resolve modes, entity nodes with NFKC casefold ids, kin/possessive resolution against the speaker (I54), window coreference in the extractor prompt. Entity leg (S13, S32) is inert until the GC arm builds entities.
areas.gap: The ladder is at least as complete as any surveyed engine. The one signal MemSpine lacks that a surveyed engine uses is context overlap (shared neighbours, co-occurrence, temporal proximity) as a merge score. LoCoMo has a near-fixed cast, so the effect there is small; it matters for open-cast benchmarks (OP-Bench, MAB, BEAM).

engine_table.approach: Rule-based, no LLM: pg_trgm candidates; score = 0.5 name similarity + 0.3 selectivity-weighted co-occurrence + 0.2 temporal proximity (7-day decay); merge at >= 0.6
Speaker always the first node; deterministic exact/fuzzy first with an entropy gate on short names; LLM dedupe only for holdouts; edge dedupe search restricted to edges between the same entity pair
spaCy mentions (no LLM); merge on exact normalised text or top-1 cosine >= 0.95; entity-to-memory back-pointers only
Deterministic name-based ids merge same-name entities; fuzzy merge is an explicit memify pipeline (0.85)
Peers only (client-declared); aliases are free text in the peer card
sha256 of lower-cased alphanumerics; non-Latin names collapse to one empty key (defect)
Atomic memories resolve ambiguous references inside a chunk; no entity table described
Ladder: exact, alias table, top-15 embedding candidates, entropy gate, MinHash Jaccard >= 0.9, then one resolve_entity@batch call per 50 names; trust-gap merges become contested; GLiNER2 option

areas.title: 3. Temporal normalisation: absolute dates, event time versus record time
areas.question: Which clocks does a record carry, and how is time used at read?
areas.memspine_has: Three clocks (S48), W2-14 temporal anchoring, `read.temporal_relative`/`temporal_infer_year`/`temporal_leg_event_dates` (S24/S62/S63), I79 annotator, I57 date repair, I76 duration solver, E05 milestones.
areas.gap: MemSpine has the richest clock set. Missing: a precision tag and an ongoing/completed status next to the event time (Mem0 platform), a referenced-date versus observation-date split in the rendered line (Mastra), and an in-window semantic selection with a proximity boost instead of a hard span filter (Hindsight).

engine_table.approach: Every observation carries observation date, referenced date (date inside the content) and a computed relative offset; grouped under dated headings

Separate temporal pass reads each new memory with its source conversation and date: event time, ongoing versus completed, precision, memory type (event, state, plan, preference, relationship, absence)
documentDate (source authored) and eventDate (event happened) on each memory
event_date, occurred_start/end, mentioned_at, created_at; temporal arm = window overlap, semantic choice inside the window, proximity boost +/-10% at rerank
Bi-temporal edges valid_at/invalid_at/created_at/expired_at from a reference time; the formatted context printed to the reader omits the validity dates
Timestamp leaf nodes normalised to YYYY, YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD; TEMPORAL search: one LLM call extracts a query interval, rerank by date-window overlap
Session date stored on every event and value; relative dates resolved by the reader from the conversation date
LLM occurred_at; query temporal phrase parsed by rules into a date range relative to wall-clock now (not the conversation date)
reference_time declared on the request but never read in the OSS tree
valid_from/valid_to/recorded_at/superseded_at, as_of reads, absolute-span temporal leg (relative spans opt-in), read-time [= date], duration and milestone solvers (harness)

areas.title: 4. Personal profile and attributes with history
areas.question: Is there a per-user profile, how is it updated, and does it keep history?
areas.gap: The card is built but unread; standing answers and histories exist but are unscreened on a keyed-state arm. Only Mnemon and Memobase keep dated values; MemMachine and MIRIX destroy old values (documented defect).

engine_table.approach: Profile slots topic/sub_topic/content with dates; separate event timeline with gists; buffer flush at about 1,024 tokens or 1 h idle, never in the hot path
Peer card per observer-observed pair; 4 prefixes (IDENTITY/ATTRIBUTE/RELATIONSHIP/INSTRUCTION), 200 chars x 40 entries, written only by the dream deduction specialist
Profile features (category, tag, feature, value) over 37 fixed tags; update shows up to 50 old features and the LLM returns ADD/DELETE; consolidation once 20+ per tag; old values destroyed
Per-owner profile (explicit_info, implicit_traits) via add/update/delete/none ops, 60-item cap; the LoCoMo run extracts it but never reads it
Changeable values keyed 'thing . attribute' with dated history and a conflict flag; directives shown first
Core blocks human/persona (5,000 chars) rewritten by an agent, always injected
Agent-curated topic markdown files; no profile object in HEAD
profile_card_v2 (no read consumer, S46 skipped), standing answers for keyed state facts (S34), value histories (S42), persona pinned

areas.title: 5. Session, topic and episode summaries
areas.question: What higher-level units exist, who produces them, and what is retrieved?
areas.memspine_has: S01/S31/S33/S61/S64 queued; call-2 content (stitched narrative) still a stub.
areas.gap: Two ideas are not in MemSpine: (a) render the parent summary next to each retrieved fact; (b) a stable, dense, always-in-context log instead of retrieval, the Mastra design, which reports 84.2 (gpt-4o) to 94.9 (gpt-5-mini) on LongMemEval-S and keeps the prefix cacheable.

engine_table.approach: LLM topic episodes (2-15 turns), title + narrative + event timestamp; merge of same-event episodes; top-2 episodes also expose raw turns to the reader
Episode per cell; summary field (200-character slice in the pinned version); retrieved unit = episode, facts nested
Rolling recursive summaries every 20 messages (<=1,500 tokens) and 60 (<=6,000); degenerate output (<35% distinct 4-grams) rejected
Short-term rolling summary replaces evicted turns
Rolling conversation summary, overwritten each update, attached to recalled facts through the fact-mention table
120-200-word window summary copied into the 'background' of each fact; no summary node
Session summary 250 words updated each user turn; full rebuild every 20; user summary from 10 episodes
Cross-event summaries over time windows from 15 related seeds, 200-350 words, in a separate collection (manual call)
No retrieval: observations replace history; Reflector condenses past a second threshold
session_close_v2: summary + episodes per closed session (>=3 turns), extractive fallback, idempotent by membership fingerprint; episode_leg_v2 lifts episode hits to member turns

areas.title: 6. Linking new facts to old ones
areas.question: How is a new fact connected to what is already stored (dedupe, supersede, extend, graph link)?
areas.memspine_has: par(m) lineage, ladder, extract_graph (sleep), neighbours_v2 (temporal neighbours only), fact chain at read (E01, opt-in).
areas.gap: Two gaps. (1) No LLM-free semantic/temporal link table over facts to expand from seeds (Hindsight), so multi-evidence recall depends on extract_graph LLM calls. (2) G-W4: the extractor does not see keys of earlier facts, so same-key supersession is not model-driven.

engine_table.approach: Top-10 existing memories shown to the extractor; the extractor's linked_memory_ids are never read; exact-text MD5 dedupe
Predict-calibrate: the episode retrieves top-10/20 existing facts; the model predicts the episode from them; extraction keeps only what the prediction missed
Per new note: LLM picks links among top-k neighbours, then 'memory evolution' rewrites the neighbours' context and tags
memory_links: temporal (<=24 h, weight 1-gap/24h), semantic kNN (top 50, cos >= 0.7), caused_by from the extraction call; expansion = tanh(0.5 x shared entities) + link weights
New memory linked to existing by updates / extends / derives; isLatest keeps retrieval on the current fact
CAUSE/CONDITION/RELATE/CONFLICT edges; top-5 neighbours above 0.8 LLM-judged contradictory, redundant or independent
Fold prompt lists existing threads and every state key with its latest value; the model reuses ids and repeats a key to record a change
Edge candidate search restricted to the same entity pair; LLM returns duplicate and contradicted indices; deterministic interval rule invalidates
Asserted LINK + lineage DAG; conflict ladder (13 rungs); entity graph in sleep; G-W4 (extractor sees earlier facts) not built

areas.title: 7. Query rewriting, expansion and decomposition at read
areas.question: What happens to the question before search?
areas.memspine_has: `read.planner=llm`, `compose_rewrites`, `second_round`, `agentic_mode query|slot` (slot net -3 at about 8x cost), `read.deep_v2` sufficiency, typed query contract. No screen is queued for planner/rewrites ('no screen' in the problem map).
areas.gap: Most top engines run no rewrite on the default path; the ones that do are agentic variants whose LoCoMo gain is small (MemMachine +0.46 points for about 2x tokens). The one rewrite style MemSpine lacks and can specify exactly is a rewrite shaped like its own stored record (dated third-person fact).

engine_table.approach: Planner writes 3 searches worded as a stored record would word them plus 1 invented answering note (HyDE); a parallel need-plan lists <=3 needs, 'ALL' for count/list; the loop pages while new positives appear
Agentic: sufficiency call; if insufficient 2-3 queries (keyword, question, HyDE statement). LLM_MULTIROUND decider: up to 3 sub-queries x 3 rounds
Agent mode: ToolSelect to SplitQuery / ChainOfQuery (<=3 rewrites after sufficiency) / direct; agent 91.69 versus memory mode 91.23 on 1,540 q, 5,566 versus 2,727 tokens/q
Forced-tool call turns the conversation into ';'-separated topics plus a temporal phrase; topics become the BM25 query
TaskGoalParser: rephrased query, keys, tags, extra memories to embed; optional sub-query split
Rule router (no LLM); COT follow-ups; DECOMPOSITION; temporal interval call
Standalone reformulation from the last <=5 exchanges (unvalidated); planner emits <=2 queries + keywords; reflection optional

engine_table.engine: Mem0, Nemori, LightMem, Memori, Hindsight, Honcho
engine_table.approach: No rewriting on the default read path
Rules shape/contract, optional LLM planner subqueries, compose_rewrites, bridge hop, second round; all off in the 81.4 arm; read.hyde_leg proposed only

areas.title: 8. Multi-hop and graph traversal
areas.question: How does the engine reach evidence that the question does not name?
areas.memspine_has: graph_leg_v2/legs_v2/edge_compiler_v2 (S30, S38, S39), PPR, bridge hop, fact chain (E01), second round.
areas.gap: Surveyed engines do at most one hop; none shows a multi-hop gain on LoCoMo specifically. MemSpine already exceeds them in options, but they are all unscreened or inert on J runs.

engine_table.approach: One-hop link expansion from <=20 semantic seeds; <=200 targets per entity, 10 s timeout drops the leg; no multi-hop walk
Graph projection around vector hits, k-hop from <=10 seeds; CONTEXT_EXTENSION; NL to Cypher
Edges: BM25 + cosine + BFS depth 3, RRF; nodes optional; communities retrieved but not formatted
No graph; contextual retrieval expands timeline neighbours (expand_context 3 in the LoCoMo script); CoQ/RaRag for multi-hop
No graph; agentic cluster-scoped expansion
get_reasoning_chain walks the premise-to-conclusion DAG; no entity traversal
Bottom-up 'light-up' of topics and values linked to the View's records; re-read linked records (<=8)
Entity BFS depth 2 (cap 3), degree 50, <=10 hits, trust-gated; PPR opt-in; bridge hop; cluster expand; all off in the reference

areas.title: 9. Answer prompts: inference versus refusal
areas.question: What does the reader prompt allow when evidence is partial?
areas.memspine_has: `--retry-refusal`, `readers.py` variants (dated_world, dated_infer, grounded_detail, routed_generic), `--verify-answer`, verify-slots diagnosed, I80 gold-lint.
areas.gap: The inference-permitting vendor prompts are part of why their open-domain scores are high, and several are paired with lenient judges. MemSpine has the variants but never screened them: the two big reader classes (inference, refusal) list 'no screen'.

engine_table.approach: 7-step chain-of-thought incl. a time-calculation step; 'do not dismiss reasonable inferences'; up to 32,768 output tokens
Prefer the most recent memory on conflict, convert relative to absolute dates from memory timestamps, <= 5-6 words, step by step
Tells the model not to say no information was found
Answer from memory; exact 'not mentioned' string if unsupported; an empty context returns the abstention with no call
'I don't know' if context insufficient; question date given; start from memory titles then chunks
Verify, aggregate lists, stop after 2-3 searches, 'unknown' only after three failed searches, otherwise guess; LoCoMo-specific examples
Agent decides what to search and how often over stored files; 74.0 with gpt-4o-mini
Clean grounded prompt (post-I80), neutral refusal retry, date repair, duration solver; reader variants dated_infer / routed_generic exist but have no screen

areas.title: 10. Image and multimodal memory
areas.question: How do image turns become memory?
areas.gap: MemSpine resolves the original image at read time; every surveyed engine that handles images does it at ingest. A silent-drop path (Mem0) is the main pitfall.

engine_table.approach: With enable_vision the LLM describes image parts before extraction; without it image turns are silently dropped
Images/files inline in retain content; separate vision slot only for chunks with attachments (1,500 chars per image, <=8 per chunk); facts keep a link to the attachment
Image/file/URL parsers (markitdown, vision LLM)
Optional parser turns image/PDF/audio/video into text with a multimodal LLM
Screenshot ingestion in the paper; the accumulator is not wired into the server
LoCoMo image questions sometimes unanswerable because the BLIP caption lacks the detail
E04: dataset's own image URLs fetched once, hash-cached, vision port (qwen2.5vl:3b); read.asset_evidence cached/fetch; reader caption-line variant

areas.title: 11. World-knowledge tools
areas.question: Do memory engines call external knowledge, and where does it enter?
areas.memspine_has: E03 external evidence (off), reader prompt world-knowledge clause (`dated_world`).
areas.gap: No surveyed engine reports a web tool in a LoCoMo run; the leading open-domain scores rely on the reader's prior. MemSpine's separation of public from private evidence matches MemOS's design.

engine_table.approach: internet_search intent parsed in fine mode; web results (OuterMemory) shown in a separate block; internet leg off by default
Natural-language-to-Cypher and agentic tool loop with skills; no web tool on the default path
Tool-calling agent over its own memory only (mental models, observations, recall)
Agent-defined tools (files, search); no fixed world tool
Highest open-domain F1 49.56 / J 76.60 in the Mem0 paper table, from memory plus LLM prior, no web
E03: wikipedia provider (keyless), privacy filter, cache, call budget, separate [public knowledge] block that never proves a private fact; S23 skipped (no provider, network egress)

areas.title: 12. Conflict and knowledge update
areas.question: How are contradicted or changed facts handled, and when?
areas.memspine_has: Ladder with trust gate, retract tags, interval order, histories (S42), reconcile (S41), contest state, as-of reads.
areas.gap: MemSpine's key-scoped deterministic design avoids the whole-graph search flaw (#1728). The open risk is the optional LLM judge: Graphiti's report shows a small non-reasoning judge fails silently, and MemSpine's judge is a local 9B.

engine_table.approach: Extraction is ADD-only; both versions survive; no supersession

LLM returns contradicted indices per new edge; a deterministic rule sets invalid_at = new valid_at and expired_at = now. Known issues: a non-reasoning judge silently misses contradictions (#1666); invalidation searches the whole graph and dates retirements to ingest time (#1728)
Raw facts append-only; a consolidation LLM per batch of <=8 facts creates/updates/deletes observations: prefer update, cascade a state change, keep 'previously X, now Y'
updates / extends / derives relations; isLatest keeps retrieval on the current fact; its own report lists 100% on knowledge update
Value appended with a conflict flag; at read an LLM judge withdraws 'no longer current' records (p >= 0.5) and lists them
Offline update queue (top 10 of 20 neighbours); LLM update/delete/ignore, hard delete
Opt-in 'contradicts' edge (non-destructive) and temporal resolution for declared functional relations
Dream deduction specialist updates/deletes, old value not kept
Reflector removes superseded observations
Deterministic 13-rung ladder: NOOP/ADD/UPDATE/INVALIDATE/CONTEST, 7 rungs on by default; LLM judge escalation and cross-key invalidate opt-in

areas.title: 13. What each engine reports on LoCoMo and LongMemEval, and with which judge
areas.question: Can the numbers be compared with MemSpine's 81.4 (Qwen3.5-9B reader and judge, cat 1-4, 1,540 q)?
areas.memspine_has: Errata (47 entries), official F1 port (0 mismatches on 1,748 cases), mem0-official judge prompt flag, cluster-bootstrap CI, noise-floor tools, A1 same-model confound declared.
areas.gap: No published number shares reader, judge and question set with ours. Judges differ and several are described as lenient; the same engine moves a lot between harnesses (Zep 58-75, Mem0 77.7-92.5, Memori 41-87). MemSpine's context is the smallest of the set (672-1,571 tokens against 2.3k-36k), the one axis on which a fair claim exists.

items.problem: Derived facts are retrieved as stand-alone records and lose to raw turns; the retrieval unit and the index key are the same object. Engines that win use facts (or lossless restatements) as KEYS to a larger parent unit (episode or source chunk) and return the parent.

evidence.method: measured: stage/class labels of clean-jina-full (evals/analysis/locomo_problem_labels_clean_jina_full.txt); classes implicit_or_paraphrased_gold, vocabulary_mismatch_recall, temporal_evidence_missing, list_aggregation_generic. These are the classes where the gold line is not found by its surface form; counts include every stage the label assigns.

items.gap: No arm combines window facts as index keys with parent-window lift and MaxSim ranking; S03/S04 test facts as competing records and lose.
items.hypothesis: Rank the parent window by max similarity over its facts (MaxSim) plus the raw window, then return the parent window with its facts as annotations; this removes the fact-versus-raw-turn competition. Expected: recover part of the implicit, vocabulary and temporal recall misses on the GC sample (hypothesis +2 to +4 net), no loss on lexical questions because the raw-window leg stays.

solutions.name: Facts as keys, parent lift (EverOS VECTOR method)
solutions.generic_mechanism: Index facts; score each parent unit by the max (or heap-expanded) fact score; return the parent unit text with facts attached by parent_id.
solutions.cost: 0 extra calls at read; write cost unchanged (window_extract already runs)
solutions.risk: EverOS's own header calls the cross-encoder net negative on hybrid episodes; test with and without the Jina rerank

solutions.name: Contextual atomic memory plus attached source chunk (Supermemory)
solutions.generic_mechanism: Keep the verbatim chunk beside each atomic memory and inject both on a hit.
solutions.source: https://supermemory.ai/research/longmembench 3.1/3.4; Nemori appends raw turns of its top-2 episodes: docs/engine_survey/nemori.json#answer.shape
solutions.risk: token budget; MemSpine is at 672 tokens/q so headroom exists

items.test: New GC arm: S43 window facts + `maxsim` leg + S15 lift; screen on fail_retrieval and fail_temporal slices; compare with S62. A J run is inert (needs derived layers).

items.problem: The replay timestamp must reach the extractor for every line. Three engines silently lose it: Mem0 OSS refuses a caller timestamp and dates facts with the run date; Memori facts carry only ingest time; Nemori facts get wall-clock created_at and the reader then sees it as the fact time.

evidence.method: measured: stage/class labels of clean-jina-full (evals/analysis/locomo_problem_labels_clean_jina_full.txt); classes temporal_evidence_missing, date_wrong_event, date_offset_small. Date-bearing wrong classes; the defect itself is a code property, so the test is a unit test, not a LoCoMo effect.

items.gap: No invariant test that no derived record falls back to wall-clock time when the source turn has a session date.
items.hypothesis: A property test over the write path (fake clock far from the data dates) finds zero derived records whose valid_from or rendered date equals the wall clock; any hit is a bug that costs temporal accuracy. Expected LoCoMo effect: none if clean; protects every replayed benchmark.

solutions.name: Fake-clock invariant test
solutions.generic_mechanism: Run a window write with the clock set years after the data; assert valid_from, rendered date and annotations derive from the session date.

items.test: Unit test in tests/ with FakeClock and a fake extractor; no GPU.

items.problem: Restatement erases who said it. SimpleMem discards speaker labels; LightMem groups facts per speaker in the prompt; MemOS ingests each conversation once per speaker perspective so search sees both views.

evidence.method: measured: stage/class labels of clean-jina-full (evals/analysis/locomo_problem_labels_clean_jina_full.txt); classes speaker_confusion, distractor_line. Classes where the wrong line or wrong speaker was used (heuristic labels in the problem map).

items.gap: R14-confirmed: MemSpine's perspective layer already covers this; the only open item is the proposed 'answer provenance check' (no key yet).
items.hypothesis: R14-confirmed I59/I63. No new arm: keep the speaker in every rendered fact line and in the fact's cited span. MemOS's double-perspective ingest corresponds to our perspective leg, already in the 81.4 arm.

solutions.name: Per-speaker perspective ingestion (MemOS script) and grouped speaker blocks (LightMem)
solutions.generic_mechanism: Render evidence grouped by speaker so the reader can match the question subject.

items.test: None new; reuse the speaker_confusion/distractor slice.

items.problem: Window boundaries ignore the calendar-day or session change that the best segmenters cut on first (EverOS prompt: calendar-day change is the highest-priority split, then topic shift, task done, gap over 4 h; hard cap 65,536 tokens or 500 messages). MemSpine's topic-shift test is 'never tested across a session change'.

evidence.method: heuristic: measured on write logs only; no question set

items.gap: R14-confirmed S45: the cut order (session/day first, topic second) is only a screened-for-cost setting.
items.hypothesis: Cutting on session change before topic shift removes cross-session windows, so every fact gets one unambiguous date; measured as fewer facts_ungrounded and fewer facts whose cited lines span two dates. Cost neutral.

solutions.name: Day/session-first boundary order
solutions.generic_mechanism: Hard cut on date change; then embedding or LLM topic shift; token hard cap.
solutions.source: docs/engine_survey/evermemos.json#segment.rule; Nemori LLM rule docs/engine_survey/nemori.json#segment.rule; Honcho token gate docs/engine_survey/honcho.json#segment.rule
solutions.risk: more, smaller windows means more calls; measure calls per turn

items.test: Count cross-date windows in stored LoCoMo ingest logs (CPU) before and after S45.

items.problem: String and embedding similarity alone merge or split entities wrongly when names are short or share a surname; co-occurrence and time proximity disambiguate without a model call.

evidence.method: heuristic: no LoCoMo class depends on it; effect is on call count and open-cast sets

items.gap: No context-overlap score in the rules tier; ambiguous names go straight to the LLM batch.
items.hypothesis: Add a weighted co-occurrence and temporal-proximity term to the rules tier (Hindsight weights 0.5/0.3/0.2 as the starting point) and measure the fraction of names sent to the LLM batch; expected: fewer resolve_entity calls at equal merge precision on a hand-built alias fixture. No LoCoMo accuracy effect expected.

solutions.name: Context-weighted resolution score (Hindsight)
solutions.generic_mechanism: score = a*name_sim + b*selectivity-weighted shared-neighbour overlap + c*time proximity; merge above a threshold.
solutions.risk: thresholds tuned on one corpus; use only as a rules-tier pre-filter

items.test: Synthetic alias fixture plus the entity logs of S02; count LLM batch calls.
